items.name: Wellhead platforms & jackets
items.line: Platforms, jackets, piles and topsides, including helidecks.
items.intro: We engineer wellhead platforms from the piles up: jacket, piles, topside structure, helideck and the topside facilities, for fabrication-ready issue.
items.seoTitle: Offshore jacket & wellhead platform engineering | VDE
items.seoDescription: Jacket, pile, topside and helideck design engineering for wellhead platforms. In-place, fatigue, seismic, load-out and lift analyses. Bengaluru, India.
deliverables: Jacket, pile and topside structural design reports
Topside piping layouts, stress analysis and isometrics
Electrical and instrumentation design for topside facilities
3D model, general arrangement and IFC structural drawings

faq.q: Which codes do you design jackets and piles to?
faq.a: API RP 2A, ISO 19901 / 19902, AISC and DNV-RP-C203 for fatigue, plus the client's own standards.

faq.q: Can you engineer several similar jackets in parallel?
faq.a: Yes. For one EPC contract we delivered detail engineering of 10 platform jackets. See the case study for scope.

faq.q: Which structural software do you use?
faq.a: SACS for in-place, fatigue, seismic, load-out and lift analyses; GRLWEAP for pile drivability; STAAD.Pro and Tekla for topside structures and drawings.

faq.q: Can you support us in the tender before award?
faq.a: Yes. Pre-bid engineering covers concept, configuration, weight estimate, MTOs and material requisitions within the tender window.

image.alt: A steel platform jacket sliding off a launch barge into the sea.
image.caption: Tamar jacket launched from barge H851. Illustrative photo, not a VDE project.

what: A wellhead platform is an offshore platform built over a group of oil or gas wells. It carries the wellheads and the valves that control each well, with little or no processing on board: the well fluids go by pipeline to a process platform or to shore. Many are unmanned and visited only for maintenance, so most have a helideck for access.

The platform stands on a jacket: a welded steel lattice tower that reaches from the seabed to above the waves. Steel piles driven through or alongside the jacket legs fix it to the seabed. The topside, the deck structure on top of the jacket, carries the wellheads, piping, electrical and instrument equipment and the helideck.

how.d: Water depth, soil data, wave, wind, current and seismic criteria and the topside loads are agreed with the client.
Jacket shape, number of legs and piles and deck levels are chosen, and a first weight estimate is made.
The structure is checked for storm, fatigue and earthquake loads, and the piles for capacity and drivability.
Load-out, sea transport and lift are analysed, so the structure survives the journey offshore as well as the sea.
Piping, mechanical, electrical and instrument layouts are developed in the 3D model around the wellheads.
IFC drawings, material take-offs and weight reports go to the fabrication yard.

who.role: Designs the jacket, piles, topside structure and helideck, and runs the in-place, fatigue, seismic and installation analyses.
Lays out the wellhead and flowline piping and checks it for stress.
Specifies equipment such as cranes, pumps and vessels, and reviews vendor data.
Designs power distribution, lighting and hazardous-area equipment on the topside.
Designs the well control, shutdown and monitoring instrumentation.
Builds the 3D model where every discipline is coordinated and clashes are found before fabrication.

items.name: Process platforms
items.line: Medium to large process platforms, from FEED to IFC.
items.intro: We deliver multi-discipline engineering for medium and large process platforms: process, mechanical, piping, E&I, telecom and structural, coordinated in one 3D model.
items.seoTitle: Offshore process platform engineering services | VDE
items.seoDescription: Multi-discipline engineering for medium and large offshore process platforms: process simulation, P&IDs, piping, E&I, structural and 3D model.
deliverables: Process simulation, heat and material balances, PFDs and P&IDs
Safety studies input and relief and flare calculations
Equipment datasheets and material handling studies
Piping layouts, material specifications, stress analysis and isometrics
Electrical load lists, single-line diagrams and power system studies
Instrument datasheets, SIS and DCS architecture, I/O lists
Topside structural design and the multi-discipline 3D model

faq.q: Do you cover every discipline for a process platform?
faq.a: Yes: process, mechanical, piping, electrical, instrumentation and control, telecom, offshore structural and 3D layout are all in-house in Bengaluru.

faq.q: Can you work in our 3D model environment?
faq.a: Yes. We work in AVEVA E3D / PDMS and S3D, on our servers or on the client's system over Citrix or VPN.

faq.q: Which electrical and instrumentation codes do you apply?
faq.a: IEC 60079 for hazardous areas and IEC 61511 for safety instrumented systems, plus the project specification.

image.alt: Offshore oil production platform on a four-legged jacket, with helideck and flare boom, far out at sea.
image.caption: Production platform P9 Horizon, North Sea. Illustrative photo, not a VDE project.

what: A process platform is where the oil, gas and water coming from the wells are separated and treated before export. It is usually the hub of an offshore field: wellhead platforms send their production to it by pipeline or bridge, and it sends export-quality oil and gas on to shore or to a tanker.

On board are separators, compressors, pumps and heat exchangers, plus the utility systems that support them: power generation, cooling, fuel gas, flare and fire protection. Because the platform handles hydrocarbons under pressure, safety systems and hazardous-area design are central to the engineering. Medium and large process platforms weigh thousands of tonnes and are usually manned.

how.d: Simulations set the heat and material balances, then PFDs and P&IDs define every line, valve and instrument.
Each equipment item is sized and specified, and vendor offers are reviewed.
Relief, flare and hazardous-area studies set how the plant is protected, and the safety instrumented systems are designed.
Equipment and piping are arranged deck by deck in one 3D model, with access, escape routes and maintenance space.
The topside structure is designed for equipment weights, lifting and accidental loads.
Isometrics, cable schedules, datasheets and drawings are issued for construction.

who.role: Runs the simulations, develops the P&IDs and sets the design conditions for every system.
Sizes and specifies the rotating and static equipment and reviews vendor documents.
Designs the piping layout and material specifications, and runs stress analysis.
Designs power generation and distribution, load lists and hazardous-area equipment.
Designs the control and safety systems (DCS, SIS) and specifies every instrument.
Designs communications on board: radio, public address, CCTV and networks.
Designs the decks and the topside structure that carries the plant.
Coordinates all disciplines in the 3D model and produces the layouts.

items.name: FPSO topside modules
items.line: Process and utility modules: layouts, structure and weight control.
items.intro: We engineer FPSO topside process and utility modules: module layouts, structural design, piping and E&I, with weight control from concept to as-built.
items.seoDescription: FPSO topside process and utility module engineering: layouts, structural design, piping, E&I and weight control. Multi-discipline team in Bengaluru.
deliverables: Module structural design, including lift and transportation cases
Piping layouts, stress analysis and isometrics
Equipment datasheets and vendor document review
Module weight reports and weight control

faq.q: Do you run weight control on FPSO modules?
faq.a: Yes. We keep the module weight report current from the first estimate through detail design and as-built, and report trends against the lift and hull limits.

faq.q: Do you design the module structure as well as the facilities?
faq.a: Yes. Offshore structural covers the module frames, lift and transportation cases alongside the piping, mechanical and E&I design.

faq.q: Can you take on a single module rather than a full topside?
faq.a: Yes. Scope can be one process or utility module, a group of modules or a single discipline across all modules.

image.alt: An FPSO with lit topside modules at dusk, with offshore support vessels nearby.
image.caption: SeaRose FPSO and offshore support vessels. Illustrative photo, not a VDE project.

what: An FPSO (floating production, storage and offloading unit) is a ship-shaped vessel that produces oil and gas offshore, stores the oil in its hull and offloads it to shuttle tankers. It is used where fixed platforms are not practical, such as deep water or remote fields with no pipeline to shore.

The processing plant sits on deck in topside modules: steel-framed blocks that each hold one part of the plant, such as separation, gas compression, water injection or power generation. Modules are built on land, lifted onto the hull and connected. Because the hull moves with the waves and has deck-load limits, the weight and centre of gravity of every module must be closely controlled.

how.d: The plant is divided into modules, and each module gets its equipment list, footprint and weight budget.
Equipment and piping are arranged inside each module, with access and interfaces to the hull and neighbouring modules.
Module frames are designed for vessel motions, lifting onto the hull and sea transport.
Piping, mechanical and E&I design are completed module by module.
The weight report is updated at every stage and checked against the lift and hull limits.
Drawings, isometrics and the 3D model are issued for fabrication.

who.role: Defines the process and utility systems in each module.
Sizes and specifies the module equipment and reviews vendor documents.
Designs the piping inside each module and the connections between modules.
Designs module power distribution and hazardous-area equipment.
Designs the module instrumentation and its links to the vessel control and safety systems.
Designs the module frames for vessel motions, lifting and transport, and supports weight control.
Builds the module 3D models and checks interfaces with the hull and other modules.

items.name: Subsea pipelines
items.line: Pipelines, risers, tie-in spools and PLEMs, from sizing to as-built.
items.intro: We engineer subsea pipelines, risers, tie-in spools and PLEMs, from hydraulic sizing through detail design to as-built documentation.
items.seoDescription: Subsea pipeline, riser, spool and PLEM engineering: sizing, wall thickness, on-bottom stability, free spans, cathodic protection and as-built records.
deliverables: Pipeline sizing and flow assurance input
Alignment sheets, crossing drawings and as-built documentation

faq.q: Which pipeline codes do you work to?
faq.a: DNV-ST-F101, DNV-RP-F109 for on-bottom stability, ASME B31.4 and B31.8, plus the project and operator specifications.

faq.q: Do you cover risers and spools as well as the line pipe?
faq.a: Yes: pipelines, risers, tie-in spools and PLEMs, including stress, stability and cathodic protection design.

faq.q: Which software do you use for pipeline analysis?
faq.a: OrcaFlex and OFFPIPE for installation and dynamic analyses, DNV StableLines for on-bottom stability and PIPESIM for hydraulics.

image.alt: Red and white pipelay vessel with a yellow pipe-laying tower, moored in port.
image.caption: Pipelay vessel Sapura Jade, Rotterdam. Illustrative photo, not a VDE project.

what: Subsea pipelines carry oil, gas and water along the seabed: from wells to platforms, between platforms and from the field to shore. They are steel pipes, often with a concrete weight coating, protected from corrosion by coatings and anodes.

Where a pipeline reaches a platform, a riser takes it up the jacket to the topside. Tie-in spools are short pipe sections that connect the pipeline to the riser or to subsea equipment. A PLEM (pipeline end manifold) is a seabed structure at the end of a line where valves and connections are grouped.

how.d: Flow simulations set the pipe diameter for the expected flow rates and pressures.
The steel wall is designed for internal pressure, external collapse and buckling.
Checks show the pipe stays in place under waves and currents, and spans over uneven seabed are assessed.
Coatings and cathodic protection are designed to last the design life.
The connections at each end of the line are designed and analysed.
Pipelay is analysed, then alignment sheets and as-built records are produced.

who.role: Designs the pipeline, risers and spools: wall thickness, stability, free spans, cathodic protection and installation.
Sizes the line and provides flow assurance input.
Designs PLEMs, riser clamps and supports.
Models the route, crossings and tie-ins and produces the drawings.

items.name: Brownfield
items.line: Modifications, re-analysis and upgrades of existing platforms.
items.intro: We engineer modifications, re-analysis and upgrades for platforms already in service, starting from the as-built records and the condition of the asset today.
items.seoDescription: Brownfield engineering for existing offshore platforms: structural re-analysis, modifications, tie-ins, upgrades and as-built updates.
deliverables: Structural re-analysis of existing jackets and topsides

faq.q: Can you start from incomplete as-built records?
faq.a: Yes. We review the records the operator holds, list the gaps and agree how each gap is closed before analysis starts.

faq.q: Do you re-analyse existing jackets for new loads?
faq.a: Yes. We re-analyse existing structures in SACS for added topside loads, modified appurtenances or changed design criteria.

faq.q: Can you update our existing 3D models and drawings?
faq.a: Yes. As-built drawings and 3D models in E3D / PDMS, S3D, AutoCAD and MicroStation are a core service.

image.alt: Two long-established offshore platforms linked by a bridge, off the coast of Southern California.
image.caption: Existing production platforms, Southern California. Illustrative photo, not a VDE project.
image.credit: US Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement (BSEE)

what: Brownfield engineering is work on platforms that are already built and producing. Over a field's life, operators add wells, tie in new pipelines, replace equipment, raise production or extend the platform's service life. Every change has to fit into an existing structure and plant.

Unlike a new design, brownfield work starts from what is already there. Drawings may be out of date, the structure may have corroded or been changed, and the platform usually keeps producing while the work is done. Records review, as-built checks and re-analysis of the existing structure come first.

how.d: Existing drawings, models and inspection reports are reviewed and the gaps listed.
The current state is confirmed from surveys and the 3D model is updated.
The existing jacket and topside are checked for the new loads and their present condition.
New equipment, piping, tie-ins and structural changes are designed to fit the existing plant.
Work is packaged so it can be installed offshore with as little shutdown as possible.
As-built drawings, models and weight data are updated for the operator.

who.role: Re-analyses the existing jacket and topside and designs strengthening and new supports.
Designs tie-ins and piping modifications into live systems.
Checks how each change affects the existing process systems.
Designs electrical modifications and checks the load on existing supplies.
Modifies the control, shutdown and instrument systems.
Updates the as-built 3D model and drawings.

items.name: Offshore wind
items.line: HVDC and HVAC offshore substation (OSS) jackets and topsides.
items.intro: We apply our oil and gas platform experience to offshore substation (OSS) platforms: jacket and topside structures for HVAC and HVDC substations.
items.seoTitle: Offshore substation (OSS) jacket & topside design | VDE
items.seoDescription: Offshore wind substation (OSS) engineering for HVAC and HVDC platforms: jacket and topside structural design and optimisation.
deliverables: OSS jacket and topside structural design

faq.q: Have you engineered offshore substation platforms?
faq.a: Yes. We optimised the OSS jacket and topside for the Taean offshore wind farm. See the case study for scope.

faq.q: Do you cover both HVAC and HVDC substations?
faq.a: Our offshore wind scope covers HVAC and HVDC offshore substation platforms.

faq.q: How does oil and gas platform experience transfer to OSS?
faq.a: The jacket, pile, load-out and lift engineering is the same discipline. The topside layout is driven by the electrical equipment instead of process equipment.

image.alt: Offshore electrical substation topside and jacket on a transport barge, pulled by a tug.
image.caption: Offshore substation ROW01-Z01 (33/220 kV) on barge Caroline. Illustrative photo, not a VDE project.

what: An offshore wind farm needs an offshore substation (OSS) to collect power from its turbines and send it to shore. The substation steps up the voltage (HVAC) or converts alternating current to direct current (HVDC), so the power can travel long distances by export cable with low losses.

The substation sits on a platform much like an oil and gas platform: a steel jacket piled to the seabed and a topside holding transformers, switchgear and, for HVDC, converter equipment. The topside is heavy, and its layout is driven by the electrical equipment and the cooling, fire protection and access around it.

how.d: Site, metocean and soil data, and the electrical equipment list and weights, are agreed.
Transformers, switchgear and support systems are arranged in the topside and the 3D model.
The jacket and topside are designed for storm, fatigue and earthquake loads.
Steel weight is cut while meeting every code check, which lowers fabrication and installation cost.
Load-out, transport and lift are analysed.
Weight reports and construction drawings are issued.

who.role: Designs and optimises the jacket and topside, and runs the in-place, fatigue, seismic and installation analyses.
Provides the electrical equipment layout and interfaces for transformers and switchgear.
Builds the 3D model and the equipment layout.
